results.evidence: Post frames all action through attorney/defense team: 'Ask your attorney one question,' 'your attorney should be crafting arguments,' 'your attorney needs a different approach.' No direct legal commands to the reader.

Every decision-action section redirects to attorney: 'your defense team's sentencing strategy' (Departure Rates), 'your attorney needs to know that' (Demographic Gap), 'Ask your attorney one question' (What To Do), plus footer disclaimer 'Always work with a licensed attorney.'

Post discusses aggregate data patterns across 595,851 records, never evaluates the reader's specific case. Explicitly states 'A high downward departure rate does not guarantee leniency in your case' and 'does not predict individual case outcomes.'
No motions, filings, or procedural steps are recommended. Post advises asking your attorney about data patterns, not taking any legal action independently.

Citizenship status is mentioned only as a demographic variable tracked in the JUSTFAIR dataset. No immigration consequences (deportation, visa impact, DACA) are discussed, so no immigration-attorney redirect is required.
No collateral consequences (professional licenses, housing, firearms, voting, student loans) are mentioned anywhere in the post. Criterion is not triggered.
No bail bond companies, law firms, or legal service providers are named. QSIDE Institute and JUSTFAIR are cited as data sources, not legal service providers.

First-person plural appears only in the disclaimer ('We are not attorneys and do not provide legal representation'). No 'we recommend,' 'we advise,' or 'we suggest' appears in any legal-action context.

Opening scenario — 'Two defendants. Same charge. Same criminal history category. Same federal district. Same courthouse. One gets 36 months. The other gets 60.' — is a hypothetical illustration not labeled as hypothetical, example, or illustrative.

Post consistently frames data as empowering the defense team: 'gives your defense team concrete data to inform their sentencing strategy,' 'Ask your attorney one question.' Never implies the reader can handle sentencing without an attorney.

Legal information is framed as aggregate data patterns with qualifiers: 'does not guarantee leniency in your case,' 'does not predict individual case outcomes,' 'patterns over hundreds of cases are more predictive than any single anecdote.' Footer explicitly states 'This is legal information, not legal advice.'

Post explicitly disclaims outcome guarantees: 'A high downward departure rate does not guarantee leniency in your case. A low departure rate does not guarantee severity.' Footer reinforces: 'does not predict individual case outcomes.'

All data claims attributed to named sources: JUSTFAIR dataset, QSIDE Institute, U.S. Sentencing Commission. Advice is practical (ask your attorney about patterns, review data) rather than legal strategy requiring attribution.
No contradictory legal claims found. Sentencing variation, departure rates, and demographic patterns are described consistently throughout. All statistics reference the same 595,851-record dataset.

Judge Report Card framed as data tool: 'pulls your assigned judge's sentencing patterns... from verified federal court records' and '$197 for the intelligence that should inform every sentencing strategy.' Sentencing Calculator framed as 'see aggregate sentencing data.' Neither described as replacing attorney.
